How it works

One chain from an idea to recorded, verified work, drawn once. Every stage, every gate, every way back and every place a goal is set aside is on the diagram below.

In plain words
  • A goal is one piece of work with a clear finish line.
  • Every goal goes through the same seven phases: restate it, look at the code, plan, have the plan reviewed, build it test-first, review it, then reflect on it.
  • If a reviewer is not satisfied, the work goes back a step. If a decision needs a person, the goal is set aside with a reason and the run moves on.
  • If you start from a raw idea, an optional front end turns it into goals first. An optional gate can refuse to work a goal that has not been mapped onto the code.
  • Nothing is called done until the record shows the phases ran. Some of that is checked by code and some is an instruction to the agent; Trust and limits says which.

The whole flow

Dashed boxes are exits and optional steps. Dashed lines are ways back or out. The design gate (highlighted) is off by default; see The design gate.

Stage by stage

StageWhat it doesCommand
DossierCaptures a raw idea as one ticket, through eight fixed questions. It reads no code./sigma-dossier, or /sigma-prd-intake for a requirements file
Goal DesignMaps the idea (or an undesigned goal) onto the real code and writes the result to a design file./sigma-goal-design
Goal ReviewA separate pass confirms or rejects the design. Only a confirmation marks the goal designed and creates the slices./sigma-goal-review
BacklogGoals waiting to be worked: local files or GitHub issues labelled sdlc:goal./sigma-scope, /sigma-status
Seven phasesGoal, Research, Plan, Plan-Review, Implement, Review, Retro./sigma-goal (you approve each gate), /sigma-loop (unattended)
LandVerify with fresh evidence, commit, open a pull request, review it again, merge, record.part of the loop
Technical detail

What happens at a pick

  1. The loop claims a goal. It never takes one with an open prerequisite, one that is parked, blocked or in progress, or one another run holds.
  2. Four checks run in a fixed order, and each prints OFF, PROCEED or PARKED: duplicate, oversized, design, readiness. The order matters: an oversized and undesigned goal is split first so each child gets its own design check.
  3. On PARKED the goal is not researched and the loop takes the next one. A park counts as one iteration.
  4. Each phase then runs as its own subagent at a model tier chosen for the goal. Research sizes the goal as small, medium or large; Plan-Review runs in full at every size.
CheckDefaultIf it fires
DuplicateOffParks, with the reason
OversizedOff; log-only when enabledLogs, parks or files child tickets, depending on its mode
Design gateOffParks and files a design ticket
ReadinessOn, warns onlyWarns and goes on; can be set to park

Ways back

  • Plan-Review to Plan. A send-back returns the plan for revision, then it is reviewed again.
  • Review to Implement. A send-back returns the work to be fixed and re-verified.
  • Tier escalation. A send-back the current model tier cannot resolve moves the work to the next tier up, rather than parking on "budget".
  • Post-PR review. It has a cap on cycles; at the cap the goal parks.
  • Design loop. A rejected design, or a goal the gate parked, goes back to Goal Design. Nothing re-runs a rejected design automatically; a person acts on the findings.

Ways out

OutcomeMeaningHow it resumes
ParkedNeeds a human decisionAppears in the review queue; /sigma-unpark records the decision and restores the goal
FailedNeeds a fix, not a decisionFix, then re-queue
DoneRecorded with fresh verification evidenceFinal

The loop is told to park rather than run an irreversible or paid action unattended. That is an instruction to the agent; a code check exists only when the hard-stops rule is switched on, and it is off by default.

What code enforces

The phase-record gate ships on: a goal cannot be recorded done unless the action log shows research, plan, an approved plan-review, implement, an approved review and retro. A trivial goal may waive research and retro only, and the waiver is recorded. Plan, plan-review, implement and review are never waivable.

Not measured: the whole chain, front end included, was run once end to end on a throwaway repository. That is one run, not a rate. The unattended landing path from a cloud container is covered by fakes only.
